references.text: Earlier in the chapter, the same instruction is given not to sow or harvest during the sabbatical year, which also applies to the Jubilee year.
The preceding verse introduces the Jubilee year as the fiftieth year and provides context for the rules in verse 11.
The following verse continues the description of the Jubilee year as holy and explains that the people shall eat from what grows naturally in the fields.
The law of the sabbatical year in Exodus also gives instructions to let the land rest and not harvest.
Instructions about harvesting and what grows on its own in the field, related to care for the poor.
The release year in Deuteronomy is thematically connected to the Jubilee principles of rest and liberation.
Isaiah prophesies about the Lord's year of favor, which is theologically linked to the Jubilee's themes of liberation and restoration.
Ezekiel mentions the release year in connection with land distribution, which relates to the rules of the Jubilee year.
Jesus quotes Isaiah 61 and proclaims the Lord's year of favor, fulfilling the spiritual significance of the Jubilee.
